chapter: New Orleans musicians, recordings and radio
title: MCA's offer to renew a copyright and signing away rights
summary: MCA recently asked her to sign away all rights to "You've Got to Reap What You Sow"; she showed it to a lawyer at AGAC and renews her own copyrights.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Yes, they're bootlegging today, right? Now they're bootlegging. You know, I had a letter from this man at MCA -- what's his name up there at Columbia?
No, not John. The other man -- what's his -- the other man. I can't think of --

Anyhow, I had a letter from him. At first the young man called me and said that they wanted to go -- they were going to renew You've Got to Reap What You Sow. So -- and sent me a thing for me to sign. You sign away your -- all rights. How stupid do they --
How stupid do they think I am -- all rights. You sign away all rights.

MCA -- not Columbia -- MCA. And, of course, I told them no. I said, if I sign away all my rights, I don't get anything? Nothing at all? See? So -- in fact, they wanted to let them renew the copyright. So, of course, I belong to AGAC and ASCAP. So I went immediately to AGAC, and I had the lawyer up there read it.

You know, he said -- I said, of course, you don't need to tell me not to sign it because I'm too smart to sign a contract like this anyhow, but I just wanted you to see it, see? So I didn't hear any more from him, from this man.
So I beat them -- I beat them to all my songs because AGAC, they always send me notice when the copyrights are due, and I send the money in right away so they can get my copyrights for me.
